source: American Geriatrics Society 2023 Beers Criteria for Potentially Inappropriate Medication Use in Older Adults
citation: 2023 American Geriatrics Society Beers Criteria Update Expert Panel. American Geriatrics Society 2023 updated AGS Beers Criteria for Potentially Inappropriate Medication Use in Older Adults. J Am Geriatr Soc. 2023;71(7):2052-2081. https://doi.org/10.1111/jgs.18372
notes: Use in adults ≥65 years. 'Avoid' = do not use unless no safer alternative. 'Use with caution' = monitor closely. This is a representative subset; see full 2023 criteria for complete list.

rules.rationale: Highly anticholinergic; increased risk of confusion, dry mouth, constipation, and other anticholinergic effects/toxicity. Diphenhydramine: increased risk of confusion, urinary retention, and impaired driving.
Not recommended for prevention of extrapyramidal symptoms with antipsychotics; more effective agents available for treatment of Parkinson disease.
Highly anticholinergic, uncertain effectiveness.
Highly anticholinergic; sedating; orthostatic hypotension.
Highly anticholinergic; uncertain effectiveness in those with dementia. Oxybutynin: lower risk with transdermal formulation.
rules.recommendation: Avoid in older adults with or at high risk for delirium, dementia, or cognitive impairment

rules.rationale: High risk of orthostatic hypotension and associated harms; not recommended as routine treatment for hypertension.
High risk of adverse CNS effects; may cause bradycardia and orthostatic hypotension; not recommended as routine treatment for hypertension.

rules.category: Cardiovascular — Digoxin for first-line atrial fibrillation or heart failure
rules.rationale: Should not be used as a first-line agent for atrial fibrillation or heart failure. Decreased renal clearance may increase risk of toxicity.
rules.recommendation: Avoid as first-line therapy for AF or HF; if used, keep serum level <0.8 ng/mL

rules.rationale: Potential for hypotension; risk of precipitating myocardial ischemia.
Effective for maintaining sinus rhythm but has greater toxicities than other antiarrhythmics used in atrial fibrillation; may be reasonable first-line therapy when rate control cannot be achieved.
rules.recommendation: Avoid as first-line therapy for atrial fibrillation unless patient has HF or substantial LVH

rules.rationale: Increased risk of stroke and mortality in persons with dementia. Avoid antipsychotics for behavioral problems of dementia or delirium unless nonpharmacological options have failed and patient is a threat to themselves or others.
rules.recommendation: Avoid for behavioral problems of dementia or delirium unless safer alternatives have failed or are not possible; avoid antipsychotics in patients with Parkinson disease or Lewy body dementia

rules.rationale: Older adults have increased sensitivity to benzodiazepines and slower metabolism; increased risk of cognitive impairment, delirium, falls, fractures, and motor vehicle accidents.

rules.category: CNS — Non-benzodiazepine, benzodiazepine receptor agonist hypnotics (Z-drugs)
rules.rationale: Adverse events similar to benzodiazepines in older adults (e.g., delirium, falls, fractures); increased emergency department visits/hospitalizations; motor vehicle accidents; may be more effective in the short-term than benzodiazepines.
Potential for cardiac problems and contraindicated in men with prostate cancer.
rules.recommendation: Avoid unless indicated for confirmed hypogonadism with clinical symptoms

rules.rationale: Chlorpropamide: prolonged half-life; can cause prolonged hypoglycemia; causes SIADH. Glyburide/glimepiride: higher risk of severe prolonged hypoglycemia in older adults.
Can cause drug-induced parkinsonism, tardive dyskinesia, extrapyramidal effects.
rules.recommendation: Avoid unless for gastroparesis with duration of use not to exceed 12 weeks except in rare cases

rules.rationale: Risk of Clostridioides difficile infection and bone loss/fractures with long-term use.
rules.recommendation: Avoid scheduled use for >8 weeks unless for high-risk patients (e.g., oral corticosteroids or chronic NSAID use), erosive esophagitis, Barrett esophagitis, hypersecretory condition

rules.rationale: Increases risk of GI bleeding/peptic ulcer disease, acute kidney injury, and fluid retention. Upper GI ulcers, gross bleeding, or perforation in 1% of patients treated for 3-6 months, and in 2%-4% of patients treated for 1 year. Use with caution if PPI or misoprostol is prescribed.
rules.recommendation: Avoid chronic use unless alternatives are not effective and patient can take a PPI or misoprostol

rules.rationale: Most muscle relaxants are poorly tolerated by older adults because of anticholinergic adverse effects, sedation, increased risk of fractures; effectiveness at doses tolerated by older adults is questionable.
Oral analgesic not effective in doses commonly used; may cause neurotoxicity (seizures); safer alternatives available.
Anticholinergic effects; increased risk of confusion and psychomotor impairment.

rules.category: Drug-drug interactions — Warfarin + NSAIDs or aspirin (>325 mg/day)
rules.rationale: Increases risk of bleeding.
rules.recommendation: Avoid combination; if NSAID necessary, use PPI

rules.category: Drug-drug interactions — 3 or more CNS-active drugs
rules.rationale: Increased risk of falls and fractures.
rules.recommendation: Avoid concurrent use of 3 or more CNS-active drugs

rules.rationale: Anticholinergic properties antagonize effectiveness of acetylcholinesterase inhibitors.
